purpose: Agent-oriented implementation specification for emulating the IBM PS/2 Model 25 (8525-8086) and Model 30 (8530-8086).

included: model-specific physical wiring that changes emulation

evidence_policy.primary: IBM Technical References, IBM BIOS interface reference, IBM option announcements, ROM bytes, disk-image bytes, and Model 30 schematics.
evidence_policy.secondary: Ardent Tool planar/MCGA notes and the archived VOGONS BIOS reverse-engineering discussion. Secondary claims are explicitly marked.
evidence_policy.citation_format: PDF citations name the corpus source_id and one-based physical PDF page. HTML citations name the repository path and original line range where available.
evidence_policy.ocr_warning: model30_techref and model30_schematic records are OCR. Verify ambiguous part numbers or single characters against page images; behavioral prose and tables were cross-checked where called out.

dma.critical_difference: None - both models share the standard XT page-register map (0x81=ch2, 0x82=ch3, 0x83=ch1, 0x87=ch0). The Model 30 TR Figure 1-8 prints a shifted map (0x80=ch2, 0x81=ch3, 0x82=ch1, 0x87=ch0), but the 8530's own BIOS and diagnostics only ever program the XT addresses, and live INT 13h DMA tests with buffers above 64 KiB land correctly only with the XT decode; the shifted map crashes both machines. The TR figure is a documentation error: its channel-1/2/3 rows are shifted one port while channel 0 stays at 0x87 (an internally inconsistent pattern).
dma.citation: model25_techref physical page 26; model30_techref physical page 27 (printed shifted map, contradicted by ROM and live DMA test); 8525/8530 BIOS rev 0 disassembly (out 0x81 for FDC/ch2, out 0x82 for HDC/ch3); live DMA probe 2026-08-03; model30_schematic physical pages 6 and 8

irq1_dispatch_contract.entry: custom controller vectors shared IRQ1 sources to INT 71h independently of the programmed normal PIC base
irq1_dispatch_contract.keyboard: BIOS copies selected port data to 0x60 and invokes programmed PIC-base + 1 handler
irq1_dispatch_contract.pointing_device: BIOS copies selected port data to 0x60 and invokes INT 73h

irq1_dispatch_contract.scan_codes: There is no 8042 translation. Operate the keyboard in scan-code set 1.

high_signal_differences: Model-specific CPU0.DGS, DTMEDTE.COM, DISK2.DGS, STG0.DGS, and SERVICES.COM binaries differ.

The Model 25 DTMEDTE.COM is larger and tests a system feature bit / uses a DOS-time fallback before RTC INT 1Ah functions; the Model 30 utility calls RTC services directly. This independently supports 'no hardware RTC on 8525'.
The Model 30 fixed-disk diagnostic contains an 'IBM HARDFILE TYPE 000' marker and is substantially larger than the Model 25 counterpart.

implementation_invariants: Machine kind must be a first-class configuration value; do not implement 8525 as a cosmetic 8530 alias.
8525 must not decode RTC ports 0xB0-0xBF or 0xE0-0xEF and must report INT 15h/C0 feature byte 1 bit 5 clear.
8530 must decode its battery-backed MM58167 register banks, route alarm as a shared IRQ1 source, and report feature byte 1 bit 5 set.
Use the model-specific DMA page-register map; this is an easy silent corruption bug.
Use custom IRQ1/INT 71h demultiplex behavior and PS/2 scan-code set 1; do not insert an AT 8042 or a second PIC.
Keep the integrated-device enables at port 0x65 functional so disabled planar decodes fall through to the I/O channel.
Represent 8525 launch RAM as 512 KiB plus optional 128 KiB; represent 8530 launch RAM as soldered 640 KiB. Both still implement port 0x6B remap/parity behavior.
Represent 8525 display as integrated 14-pin analog monitor configuration and 8530 as external 15-pin monitor-sense configuration.
The 44-pin fixed-disk interface is IBM-specific, not ATA/IDE despite later similar form factors.
